content.guideline_title: 2024 Perioperative Cardiovascular Management for Noncardiac Surgery Guideline

sections.title: Pulmonary Artery Catheters
main_points: The use of pulmonary artery catheters is associated with mixed results in terms of reducing mortality in severely ill patients.
Outcomes for patients with acute heart failure may not significantly improve with routine use of these catheters.
The evaluation of hemodynamic parameters such as pulmonary artery pressure can help inform patient management strategies.

sections.title: Perioperative Anemia Management
main_points: Optimizing anemia management includes considering intravenous iron supplementation and erythropoiesis-stimulating agents.
Transfusion strategies should be tailored to individual patient needs based on hemoglobin thresholds and clinical symptoms.

recommendations: Consideration should be given to the cost and effectiveness of pulmonary artery catheterization in various clinical settings.
Use of early treatment strategies for managing acute transfusion-related complications should be employed.
Incorporate evidence-based approaches to anemia management for improved surgical outcomes.
